subject: community-medicine
title: Outbreak investigation and surveillance

steps.tx: An **epidemic** signals a shift in the balance between agent, host and environment. Investigation aims to define its magnitude by time, place and person, find the causative factors, identify the cause and recommend prevention. The first step is **verification of diagnosis**, done on the spot and quickly. A clinical look at a sample of cases may suffice, and laboratory results should not delay the epidemiological work.

vis.alt: Two triangles joining agent, host and environment. Left triangle balanced: disease at its expected level. Right triangle tipped by a heavier agent corner: an epidemic follows.
vis.caption: Epidemics start when one corner of the triad shifts: a new agent, weaker hosts, or a changed environment.

steps.tx: Once the diagnosis is verified, confirm that the epidemic truly exists by comparing current frequency with the same period in previous years. An **epidemic threshold** is an arbitrary limit set at two standard errors above the endemic level. Then define the **population at risk**, obtaining a map of the area and calculating an appropriate denominator.

steps.tx: Define key case terms. The **index case** is the first case that comes to the attention of the investigator or clinician, and it need not be the true first case. The **primary case** is the first case introduced into the population being studied. Secondary cases arise from the primary case. The **incubation period** runs from entry of the organism to first signs, and the median incubation is the time by which half of cases appear.

steps.tx: **Surveillance** is the continuous scrutiny of factors affecting occurrence and distribution of disease. **Passive surveillance** relies on cases reported to the health system, and most Indian national programmes use it. **Active surveillance** collects data by going out to the community, as with house-to-house malaria slide collection under NVBDCP. **Sentinel surveillance** uses selected sites to find missing cases and supplement notifications, as in the National AIDS Control Programme.

points: Health system goes to the community

steps.tx: Monitoring is the routine measurement and analysis aimed at detecting changes in environment or health status, whereas surveillance is the continuous scrutiny of disease occurrence. Under IDSP, **regular surveillance** covers diseases such as malaria, cholera, typhoid, tuberculosis, measles and polio, but not road traffic accidents. For NCDs, the WHO **STEPS** approach measures risk factors through questionnaire, physical and biochemical steps.
